week_1.text:
How Synter manages campaigns across 7+ ad platforms with a single API call.

Under the hood, each platform has its own quirks:

• Google Ads requires EU political advertising flags and explicit network settings (API v21+)
• LinkedIn uses Rest.li 2.0 — not standard REST — with strict URL encoding
• Reddit's v3 API wraps every payload in {"data": {...}} and requires a custom User-Agent header
• X (Twitter) still uses OAuth 1.0a while everyone else moved to OAuth 2.0
• Meta blocks write operations without Standard Access app review

Synter abstracts all of this. One unified interface. One set of credentials. One conversation.

The agent handles token refresh, rate limiting, pagination, and platform-specific field mapping. You just say "launch a search campaign targeting SaaS founders" and Synter figures out the rest.

We built this because no marketer should need to memorize 7 different API specifications.

#AdTech #APIs #DeveloperExperience

week_2.text:
Building campaign creation that actually works across platforms is harder than it looks.

Here's what we learned:

Google's Performance Max requires a bulk mutate request — you can't create the campaign, asset group, and assets separately. Everything has to go in one atomic operation or the API rejects it.

LinkedIn deprecated the /targeting field in v202510. You now need targetingCriteria with a nested AND/OR structure. Oh, and the objective is WEBSITE_VISIT (singular), not WEBSITE_VISITS.

Reddit's CONVERSIONS campaigns need optimization_goal set on the ad group, but pixel_id is NOT a valid field (despite what you'd expect). That one took us a few hours to debug.

Every one of these edge cases is now handled inside Synter. You describe what you want — Synter handles the platform gymnastics.

We're sharing these learnings because the industry needs better tooling, and pretending cross-platform ad management is simple doesn't help anyone.

#BuildInPublic #AdTech

The teams that win will be the ones that test fastest. AI agents make that possible.

week_2.text:
Competitor analysis used to mean manually scrolling through the Facebook Ads Library and taking screenshots.

Now Synter does it in one command.

Here's the workflow:

1. Synter scrapes the Meta Ads Library for your competitor's active campaigns (via Apify — direct scraping gets blocked by Meta's bot detection)
2. Analyzes creative patterns: what hooks they're using, which formats dominate, how they structure CTAs
3. Generates NEW creatives for YOUR brand, inspired by what's working for competitors

The key insight: you're not copying ads. You're identifying patterns that perform well in your market and applying those patterns with your brand's voice and positioning.

One of our users ran this against their top 3 competitors and discovered that carousel ads with problem-agitate-solve hooks outperformed everything else in their vertical. They launched 12 variants in an afternoon.

That's the difference between insight and execution. Synter handles both.

#CompetitiveIntelligence #DigitalMarketing

week_3.text:
We added Reddit and TikTok to Synter's campaign automation. Here's what surprised us.

Reddit's v3 API is actually well-designed, but the post creation endpoint lives under /profiles/{profile_id}/posts — not under /ad_accounts/ where you'd expect it. That mismatch caused us a full day of debugging.

TikTok's Events API uses a different auth pattern than most platforms: Access-Token header (not Bearer), and the ttclid click identifier travels through context.ad.callback, not a top-level field.

The conversion tracking story is interesting too. We now send server-side events to 7 platforms in parallel: Meta CAPI, Google Offline Conversions, Reddit CAPI, LinkedIn CAPI, X CAPI, TikTok Events API, and Microsoft Ads.

Every conversion fires once. Synter fans it out to every platform that needs it. Deduplication handled via conversion_id.

This is what full-funnel, cross-platform attribution should look like — and it runs silently in the background.

#ConversionTracking #AdTech #MarTech

week_3.text:
Conversion tracking is broken — and most marketers don't realize it.

Here's the reality:

• iOS 14+ killed client-side pixel accuracy
• Cookie deprecation is making attribution worse every quarter
• Each ad platform reports different conversion numbers for the same event
• GA4 uses data-driven attribution that doesn't match any platform's self-reported numbers

The solution isn't better pixels. It's server-side event distribution.

Synter captures conversions at the server level and sends them to every platform simultaneously: Meta CAPI, Google Offline, Reddit CAPI, LinkedIn CAPI, TikTok Events API, X CAPI, and Microsoft Ads.

Same event. Same timestamp. Same user identifiers (hashed). Every platform gets first-party signal quality.

The result: more accurate attribution, better bidding algorithm performance, and lower CPAs across the board.

If you're still relying on client-side pixels in 2026, you're leaving money on the table.

#Attribution #MarTech #ConversionTracking

week_4.text:
Performance Max is Google's most complex campaign type. Here's how Synter handles it.

PMax requires an atomic bulk mutate request. You can't create the campaign first and add assets later — everything ships in one API call:

• Campaign budget
• Campaign (AdvertisingChannelType.PERFORMANCE_MAX)
• Asset group
• All asset group assets (headlines, descriptions, images, logos)

Minimum asset requirements:
— 3 headlines (30 chars each)
— 1 long headline (90 chars)
— 2 descriptions (90 chars)
— 1 landscape image (1.91:1)
— 1 square image (1:1)
— 1 logo (1:1, min 128x128)
— 1 business name (25 chars)

Synter validates all of this before the API call. If you're missing assets, it generates them. Wrong aspect ratio? It resizes. Headline too long? It rewrites.

The result: PMax campaigns that launch on the first try, every time.

This is what happens when you build advertising tools for reliability, not just features.
